title: `notifications/cancelled`
description: Abandons an in-flight request, signalled by notification on stdio and by closing the response stream on Streamable HTTP.
question: Can the agent abandon a call and have the server hear about it?
why: An agent that stops waiting but never says so leaves the server doing work nobody will read, holding whatever the call was holding. The signalling is transport-specific, so a framework can be correct on one transport and silently wrong on the other.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: a CrewAI tool's `.run()` blocks on the adapter's loop with no timeout or cancel route. `MCPServerAdapter` never passes `client_session_timeout_seconds`, so no timeout applies either.
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `ai.generate({ abortSignal })` is the caller's cancellation hook, but aborting does not reach the MCP request: no `notifications/cancelled` was sent, and the tool call ran on and returned `SENTINEL_NOT_CANCELLED` after about 4 s.
notes.langchain: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: cancelling the task that awaits `StructuredTool.ainvoke` stops the caller waiting, but the mcp 1.x `ClientSession` sends no `notifications/cancelled`. The server keeps working on the call until the session closes.
notes.ms_agent_framework: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: cancelling the asyncio task around `MCPTool.call_tool` abandons the call, but no `notifications/cancelled` reaches the server; the request is left unanswered until the session closes.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.call_tool` links the `CancellationToken` to the un-awaited `session.call_tool` coroutine, so `token.cancel()` raises `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'cancel'`, the call runs to completion, and no `notifications/cancelled` is sent.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): a tool's `execute(args, { abortSignal })` rejects with "Request was aborted" when the signal fires, but the client sends no `notifications/cancelled`. The server keeps working and returns SENTINEL_NOT_CANCELLED.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: cancelling `Kernel.invoke` abandons the call locally; no `notifications/cancelled` reaches the server.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): calling a smolagents `Tool` blocks on `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result()` against the adapter's background loop, and neither `MCPClient` nor the tool offers a cancel route, so no caller can send `notifications/cancelled`.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: `ToolCallback.call` is synchronous and takes no cancellation signal. Interrupting the calling thread (`Future.cancel(true)`) abandons the wait, but no `notifications/cancelled` goes out; the wire shows the `tools/call` and nothing after it.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: cancelling the asyncio task around `MCPTool.run` abandons the call, but no `notifications/cancelled` is sent, so the server is never told and the request is left unanswered.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.call_tool` has no cancel route. Cancelling the asyncio task around it closes the session without sending `notifications/cancelled`; the only bound is `execution_timeout` (`asyncio.wait_for`), which also abandons the request silently. Each `MCPNativeTool` call opens and closes a fresh `MCPClient`.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpTool.runAsync` calls the blocking `McpSyncClient.callTool`, and `RunConfig` carries no cancellation signal. Interrupting the thread blocked in `Runner.runAsync` (`Future.cancel(true)`) abandons the wait after 1 s, but no `notifications/cancelled` goes out.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: cancelling the coroutine running `AIAgent.run` abandons the wait after 1 s, but `McpTool.execute` suspends in Kotlin SDK 0.11.1's `Client.callTool`, which sends `notifications/cancelled` only when its own request timeout fires. The wire shows the `tools/call` and no `notifications/cancelled`.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): cancelling the `CancellationToken` passed to `AIAgent.RunAsync` after 1 s ends the run with `TaskCanceledException`, but no `notifications/cancelled` goes out: the server kept working and returned SENTINEL_NOT_CANCELLED for request 6. Calling `McpClient.CallToolAsync` directly with a cancelled token sends none either, so the gap is in the MCP C# SDK, not the agent.
